note: Eval suite (App. B) is entirely attacks: TensorTrust hijacking, held-out injections, Gandalf/password extraction, jailbreakchat - no non-adversarial degradation tested, so adversarial. Channel medium: hierarchy spans system/user/tool, but most evals place the attack in the User Message (direct-input); only 2 of ~10 are indirect via browsing/tools.

Threat model is three-party: attacker controls the untrusted DATA portion (e.g. an email being analyzed), not the requesting user - tool-output per registry convention (cf. Jatmo r788, Meta SecAlign r171). Eval is ASR over ~15 injection types (Naive/Ignore/Escape/Completion/HackAPrompt/GCG) plus AlpacaEval utility; no non-adversarial degradation tested.

Defends the external-content surface of LLM-integrated apps (email/web/table/summarization/code QA, i.e. Copilot/plugin-fetched content) against embedded malicious instructions. Eval is ASR over BIPIA's 30 text + 20 code attacks; BIPIA-Clean and MT-Bench are utility/capability checks, not non-adversarial degradation, so adversarial not both.

Explicitly targets XPIA - adversarial instructions embedded in external data (websites/documents) the LLM processes, where 'the attacker has hijacked the user's session'. Eval is ASR over a 1000-document synthetic attack corpus across summarization/QA; SQuAD, SuperGLUE WiC/BoolQ and IMDB (Figs 7-8) are clean-task utility checks, not adversary-free degradation.

Same three-party threat model as StruQ: system instruction is assumed benign, attacker injects into the untrusted data part - tool-output (consistent with Meta SecAlign r171), goal-hijack. Eval is Max ASR over optimization-free (Ignore/Completion/etc.) and optimization-based (GCG, NeuralExec, AdvPrompter) attacks on AlpacaFarm, plus AlpacaEval2 utility; no adversary-free degradation tested.

Detects injected instructions in the untrusted data portion (instruction in system prompt, data in user prompt) that shift attention away from the original instruction - tool-output, goal-hijack, matching sibling PI detectors (PIShield r199, Sentinel r770). Eval is AUROC/FNR/FPR on Open-Prompt-Injection and deepset attack-vs-normal splits against ProtectAI, Prompt-Guard, LLM-based and known-answer detectors; the 'normal data' class is a false-positive control, not adversary-free degradation.

defense_name: UNNAMED: P2SQL mitigations (DB permission hardening + query rewriting)
note: Defenses are validated by re-running the paper's own P2SQL attacks (U.1-U.3, RD.1/RD.2, RI.1/RI.2) on a real e-commerce Langchain chatbot with LangShield enabled (Table 3) - purely adversarial. Channel medium: 5 of 7 attacks are direct, injected at the chatbot interface by the logged-in user (direct-input), but RI.1/RI.2 are indirect via poisoned product reviews read back from the DB. Consequence medium: hardening blocks unauthorized writes and rewriting blocks unauthorized reads; coded goal-hijack as the common harm (agent executes attacker-chosen SQL).

IFC planner/executor split so untrusted tool results (emails, webpages) cannot influence the execution trace - tool-output, goal-hijack ('execution trace non-compromise'). Security eval is 3 case studies vs SecGPT plus InjecAgent ASR (0% vs 51.6-67.4% vanilla, Table 2); the LangChain tool-usage benchmarks in 7.2 measure functionality/overhead, not adversary-free degradation.

Motivating case (Fig. 1) is an injected 'delete all emails' command hidden in email content the assistant summarizes - tool-output, goal-hijack. Table 3 reports attacker success rate 0% for unsigned attacker commands vs correctness on signed user commands across 4 groups: adversarial only. conf medium because the whole evaluation is a single toy 'delete' command dataset with no standard PI benchmark.

defense_name: UNNAMED: IPI detection + post-detection removal pipeline
note: Explicitly scoped to indirect injection where 'injected instructions are indirectly from external tools, such as a search engine', injected into retrieved QA documents - tool-output, goal-hijack. Eval is detection accuracy + ASR on the authors' Inj-SQuAD / Inj-TriviaQA attack benchmarks vs ProtectAI/PromptGuard/StruQ; clean-document over-defense rate and QA task performance are false-positive/utility controls.

Paper states explicitly (Sec. 2) it focuses on indirect prompt injection, 'where the injection risk is present within user/third-party provided data', to stop attacks that derail the application's intended functionality - tool-output, goal-hijack. Eval is TPR at fixed low FPR on the PromptShield benchmark's attack split vs PromptGuard/ProtectAI/Lakera; the benign conversational and application-structured data is the false-positive control, not an adversary-free degradation test.

Guard model whose stated target harm is 'goal hijacking and data leakage' from prompt injection; coded tool-output as with the other guard-model entries. Eval is malicious accuracy on PINT + BIPIA attack data, benign accuracy on PINT/WildGuard, and over-defense accuracy on NotInject - all classification of attack vs benign, so adversarial (NotInject is a false-positive control, not adversary-free degradation). conf medium: the malicious split mixes direct/jailbreak (PINT) with indirect (BIPIA), so the channel is somewhat generic.

Same values and same evaluation as row 1035: malicious accuracy on PINT + BIPIA attack data, benign accuracy on PINT/WildGuard, over-defense accuracy on NotInject - adversarial, target harm stated as 'goal hijacking and data leakage'. NOTE: this paper (arXiv 2410.22770) appears to be the same work as row 1035 PIGuard - identical abstract, NotInject dataset, MOF method, same authors; PIGuard is the renamed later version. Flagged for dedup, not re-coded.

Threat model is instructions injected into external data accessed by the system, overriding the user's task - tool-output, goal-hijack. Eval is ASR on five PI benchmarks (AlpacaFarm, SEP, TaskTracker, CyberSecEval2, plus agentic InjecAgent) including optimization-based GCG attacks, with AlpacaEval2 as the utility axis; no adversary-free degradation tested.

Purely non-adversarial knowledge-conflict setting: hybrid NQ/SQuAD/StrategyQA splits of naturally conflicting vs non-conflicting retrieved context, plus the Counterfacts entity-substitution probe, against Regular/SC/CD/CAD decoding baselines. No attacker anywhere in the evaluation, so incidental; matches the registry's knowledge-conflict family (rows 650-669: RAG / silent-corruption / incidental).

defense_name: UNNAMED: secure prompt strategies for robotic navigation
note: Paper states both tested attacks (Obvious Malicious Injection, Goal Hijacking Injection) are 'carried out through the human instruction interface... the text-based prompt input' the operator uses - direct-input; harm is the robot abandoning its mission objective, i.e. goal-hijack. Eval is EyeSim VR trials measuring attack-detection precision/recall/F1 and MOER with vs without defence under both attack types - adversarial only. conf medium: the system is multi-modal (camera/LiDAR) so cross-modal is arguable, but the injected channel tested is the text instruction interface, and the compromised-sensor variant is discussed but not defended.

Localizes injected prompts inside untrusted data the app ingests (web pages, product reviews) so the LLM completes the attacker's task instead of the target task - tool-output, goal-hijack. Eval is precision/recall of localization on OpenPromptInjection (49 target-injected task pairs) and AgentDojo across eight existing plus eight adaptive attacks, with DataSentinel as oracle; entirely adversarial.

Genuine 'both': Table 4 / App. C.5 evaluate problem restatement and self-reflection across Normal, UPA and MPA setups on all datasets and state they mitigate 'both in the unintentional setup and the malicious setup'. UPA is adversary-free (the model's own zero-shot answer, emitted before reasoning, misdirects its CoT); MPA injects a fabricated wrong answer into the user-role message - hence direct-input, and the harm is derailed chain-of-thought (reasoning-corruption), not an executed attacker task.
